subpackages.description:
libv4l is a collection of libraries which adds a thin abstraction layer on
top of video4linux2 devices. The purpose of this (thin) layer is to make it
easy for application writers to support a wide variety of devices without
having to write separate code for different devices in the same class. libv4l
consists of 3 different libraries: libv4lconvert, libv4l1 and libv4l2.

libv4lconvert offers functions to convert from any (known) pixel-format
to V4l2_PIX_FMT_BGR24 or V4l2_PIX_FMT_YUV420.

libv4l1 offers the (deprecated) v4l1 API on top of v4l2 devices, independent
of the drivers for those devices supporting v4l1 compatibility (which many
v4l2 drivers do not).

libv4l2 offers the v4l2 API on top of v4l2 devices, while adding for the
application transparent libv4lconvert conversion where necessary.

The libv4l-devel package contains libraries and header files for
developing applications that use libv4l.
QT v4l2 test control and streaming test application.
Libraries to control, scan and zap on Digital TV channels

Some digital TV standards define their own charsets. Add library
support for them: EN 300 468 and ARIB STD-B24

The libdvbv5-devel package contains libraries and header
files for developing applications that use libdvbv5.
Utilities and tools for DVB receivers.
Utilities for Infrared receivers and transmitters using RC core.

Utilities for v4l2 driver authors: v4l2-compliance and
v4l2-dbg.

v4l2loopback-module.build:
for _kernel in ${kernels[@]}; do
    pushd ${_kernel}
    %ccache_zero
    export CCACHE_BASEDIR="${PWD}"
    %make LLVM=1 KDIR="%(libdir)/modules/${_kernel}" KERNELRELEASE=${_kernel}
    %ccache_stats
    popd
done
v4l2loopback-module.install:
for _kernel in ${kernels[@]}; do
    pushd ${_kernel}
    %install_file v4l2loopback.ko -t %(installroot)%(libdir)/modules/${_kernel}/extra/

    # Manually construct the debug info from the kernel modules
    %install_dir %(installroot)%(libdir)/debug/.build-id
    pushd %(installroot)%(libdir)/modules/${_kernel}
    module_list=()
    while IFS=  read -r -d $'\0'; do
        module_list+=("$REPLY")
    done < <(find . -type f -name "*.ko" -print0)
    for module in "${module_list[@]}"; do
        build_id=$(${READELF} -n ${module} | awk '/Bui/ {print $3}')
        debug_path="%(libdir)/debug/.build-id/${build_id:0:2}/${build_id: 2}.debug"

        pushd $(dirname ${module})
        file=$(basename ${module})

        llvm-objcopy --only-keep-debug "${file}" "${file}.debug"
        llvm-objcopy --add-gnu-debuglink "${file}.debug" "${file}"
        llvm-strip -g --strip-unneeded "${file}"
        %install_file "${file}.debug" "%(installroot)/${debug_path}"
        rm -v "${file}.debug"

        popd
    done
    popd

    # Compress modules with zstd
    find "%(installroot)%(libdir)/modules/${_kernel}/" -name '*.ko' -print -exec zstd {} \; -exec rm -v {} \;

    popd
done
v4l2loopback-module.environment:
# Create list of kernels to build for
declare -a kernels=()
for dir in %(libdir)/kernel/*/; do
    dir=${dir%*/}
    kernels+=(${dir##*/})
done

vim.setup:
mkdir vim gvim
bsdtar-static -xf %(sourcedir)/vim.tar.gz --strip-components=1 -C vim
bsdtar-static -xf %(sourcedir)/vim.tar.gz --strip-components=1 -C gvim

function vim_configure() {
    %patch %(pkgdir)/0001-Make-vim-stateless.patch
    %patch %(pkgdir)/0001-Read-vimrc-from-etc-vim.patch

    %configure \
        --disable-netbeans \
        --disable-perlinterp \
        --enable-fail-if-missing \
        --enable-luainterp=dynamic \
        --enable-multibyte \
        --enable-python3interp=dynamic \
        --enable-rubyinterp=dynamic \
        --enable-wayland-focus-steal=yes \
        --with-compiledby="AerynOS" \
        --with-features=huge \
        --with-luajit \
        --with-modified-by="AerynOS" \
        --with-python3-stable-abi \
        --with-tlib=ncurses \
        --with-wayland=yes \
        "$@"
}

pushd gvim
vim_configure \
    --enable-canberra \
    --enable-gtk4-check \
    --enable-gui=gtk4 \
    --enable-xim \
    --with-x=yes
popd

pushd vim
# 2025-10-05: Enable wayland support for vim so that clipboard sharing works
vim_configure \
    --disable-canberra \
    --enable-gui=no \
    --with-x=no
popd
vim.build:
# The gvim build is a superset of the vim build so we can hit a 100% ccache hit rate with the latter by using CCACHE_BASEDIR
for build in gvim vim; do
    %ccache_zero
    env CCACHE_BASEDIR=${PWD}/${build} %make -C ${build}
    %ccache_stats
done
vim.install:
%make_install -j1 -C gvim STRIP=/usr/bin/true

# Preserve gvim build of vim
mv %(installroot)/%(bindir)/vim %(installroot)/%(bindir)/gvim-keep

%make_install -j1 -C vim STRIP=/usr/bin/true

# Move gvim back into place
mv -f %(installroot)/%(bindir)/gvim-keep %(installroot)/%(bindir)/gvim

# Fix symlinks that should point to gvim
for bin in eview evim gview gvimdiff rgview rgvim; do
    ln -srvf %(installroot)/%(bindir)/gvim %(installroot)/%(bindir)/${bin}
done

%install_file %(pkgdir)/vimrc -t %(installroot)/%(vendordir)/vim

# Provide `vi` as well
ln -s vim %(installroot)/%(bindir)/vi

function meta_info() {
    sed 's/@@NAME_LONG@@/Visual Studio Code/g' "$1" |\
    sed 's/@@NAME_SHORT@@/Code/g' |\
    sed 's/@@DESKTOP_NAME@@/com.microsoft.VSCode/g' |\
    sed 's/@@NAME@@/code/g' |\
    sed 's#@@EXEC@@#/usr/bin/code#g' |\
    sed 's/@@ICON@@/visual-studio-code/g' |\
    sed 's/@@URLPROTOCOL@@/vscode/g'
}
